title: script
description: Typed Code Mode for the long tail — replaces ad-hoc bash pipelines (SDD 9.7). The source runs as a JavaScript function body in a QuickJS-ng-on-WASM guest under the Wasmtime host (SDD 8.1): fuel-metered, memory-capped, no ambient filesystem, network, or shell. The one global is `workspace`: search(args) and read(args) answer the same envelopes as the tools, glob(pattern) lists matching workspace paths — all live and jail-checked — while workspace.edit.queue({file, old, new, occurrence?, expectedHash?}) and workspace.files.queue({op: create|mkdir|delete, ...}) only QUEUE writes. An empty old populates an existing zero-byte file only; expectedHash checks the content before that queued edit. Create missing files in a separate files call before queuing edits. Use `return` for the script's JSON-serializable result value. Queued writes resolve through the 7.5 write engine and are ALWAYS confirm-gated: dryRun:true (the default) returns the value plus every dry-run diff and never applies; dryRun:false answers CONFIRM_REQUIRED with a confirmToken, and re-invoking the identical call with confirm applies. Abuse dies typed: SANDBOX_FUEL_EXCEEDED, SANDBOX_MEMORY_EXCEEDED, SANDBOX_CAP_DENIED.

source.description: JavaScript (QuickJS) function body. `workspace` is in scope; `return` a JSON-serializable value. A thrown error comes back as data (status "threw"), not a tool failure.

dryRun.description: true (default): queued writes are previewed as dry-run diffs and never applied. false: applying requires the confirm-token flow (or MRTR elicitation in-call).

confirm.description: The confirmToken from a prior CONFIRM_REQUIRED answer for this exact call (SDD 9.4). The script re-runs deterministically; matching aggregate hashes apply the queue, a changed workspace answers STALE_ANCHOR, a forged or mismatched token CONFIRM_MISMATCH.

autoApply.description: Trusted-harness bypass of the confirm gate (SDD 9.4). Prefer the confirm-token flow.

fuel.description: CPU budget per guest round. Clamps DOWNWARD from the server default — a request can narrow the sandbox, never widen it.

memoryCapBytes.description: Guest linear-memory cap in bytes. Clamps DOWNWARD from the server default (256MB).

budget.description: Token budget for the response envelope.
